lines.trans: Welcome to the Sunday Berry Cake Laboratory, apprentices! Hands washed and sleeves rolled?
Washed twice, Chef! I brought two baskets of ripe red berries and sweet almonds.
How are we going to solve the smudged blue ink at the bottom, Salma?
Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
Tin Two gets a tart lemon icing to balance the sweet ripe berries, yes?
Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.
Warm honey sounds delightfully sticky, but is it an old-fashioned local recipe?
Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!
Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
I am nervous! Who is going to taste-test them and pick the absolute winner?
We take all three straight to Mazen; his tough palate never forgives a mistake.
You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.text: بدّي أسجّل كل وصفة في الدفتر.
examples.trans: I want to write down every recipe in the notebook.
This is my grandmother's recipe for maqluba.

meanings.note: The word 'محلية' (محلية) means 'محلية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: العسل الدافي مبين دبق وبلزق بطريقة بتجنن، بس هل هو وصفة محلية قديمة؟
examples.trans: Warm honey sounds delightfully sticky, but is it an old-fashioned local recipe?
This is محلية.

meanings.note: The word 'جداتنا' (جداتنا) means 'جداتنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: جداتنا كانوا يدهنوا عسل على معجنات المكسرات من قبل ما يكون في إشي اسمه سكر فانيليا!
examples.trans: Our grandmothers brushed honey over nut pastries long before vanilla sugar existed!
This is جداتنا.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is راقبي.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Subject pronoun 'I' for any speaker.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: The word 'متوترة' (متوترة) means 'متوترة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: أنا متوترة! مين رح يذوقهم ويختار الفايز المطلق؟
examples.trans: I am nervous! Who is going to taste-test them and pick the absolute winner?
This is متوترة.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'who?' (لمين 'whose? / for whom?').

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: The word 'ناخذهم' (ناخذهم) means 'ناخذهم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: رح ناخذهم التلاتة طوالي لـ مازن؛ ذوقه الصعب عمره ما بسامح أي غلطة.
examples.trans: We take all three straight to Mazen; his tough palate never forgives a mistake.
This is ناخذهم.

meanings.note: The word 'لـ' (لـ) means 'لـ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: هادا الكتاب كان أصلا لـ رامي وعمته قبل ما يوصل لرف الإعارة!
examples.trans: This book actually belonged to Rami and his aunt before it reached the lending shelf!
This is لـ.

meanings.note: The word 'مازن' (مازن) means 'مازن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرة واحدة فوق يا مازن، وسلكك اللطيف رن مرتين متل العادة.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: In questions أي means 'which?' (أي علبة؟ 'which tin?'); in conditionals/negatives it means 'any' (أي شي 'anything').

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غلطات.

examples.trans: This is not your fault at all.
We fixed the slip-up in two minutes.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: The word 'شجاعة' (شجاعة) means 'شجاعة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is شجاعة.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: The word 'كشرة' (كشرة) means 'كشرة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is كشرة.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: The word 'نضطر' (نضطر) means 'نضطر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!

examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: The word 'وجديد' (وجديد) means 'وجديد'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: إنتي شجاعة يا سلمى. إذا عمل كشرة تلميع النحاس، رح نضطر نعيد كل شي من أول وجديد!
examples.trans: You are brave, Salma. If he makes the brass-polish face, we start all over again!
This is وجديد.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.

meanings.note: Past tense verb for bringing.

examples.trans: Here is the I brought.
I like the I brought.

meanings.note: Definite form of the color red.

examples.trans: Here is the the red.
I like the the red.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective for old.

examples.trans: Here is the old (f).
I like the old (f).

meanings.note: Definite form of sweet.

examples.trans: Here is the the sweet.
I like the the sweet.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning straight ahead or right away.

examples.trans: Here is the straight ahead / immediately.
I like the straight ahead / immediately.

meanings.note: Feminine form of light weight.

examples.trans: Here is the light (f).
I like the light (f).

meanings.note: Definite form of brass or copper.

examples.trans: Here is the the brass.
I like the the brass.

meanings.note: Noun age with his possessive pronoun.

examples.trans: Here is the his age.
I like the his age.

meanings.note: Definite feminine form of small.

examples.trans: Here is the the small (f).
I like the the small (f).

meanings.note: Almonds with conjunction and and definite article.

examples.trans: Here is the and the almonds.
I like the and the almonds.

meanings.note: Definite form of a piece of paper.

examples.trans: Here is the the single paper.
I like the the single paper.

meanings.note: Past tense plural verb for to be.

examples.trans: Here is the they were.
I like the they were.

meanings.note: Definite form of berries.

examples.trans: Here is the the berries.
I like the the berries.
